title: Cloudflare Tunnel
desc: Publish internal services to Cloudflare through cloudflared, with no public IP or open ports required
empty: No tunnels yet. Token tunnels are created in the Cloudflare Zero Trust dashboard; quick tunnels need no account
binaryPlaceholder: Leave empty to search automatically (config directory bin or PATH)
tokenHelp: Create a tunnel in the Zero Trust dashboard and copy its token; public hostnames and origin services are configured there, or here once an API token is filled in
serviceHelp: A random trycloudflare.com address is assigned and changes after a restart; suitable for temporary sharing only
protocolHelp: Choose http2 on networks that restrict UDP
apiTokenHelp: Lets you edit the tunnel's routes in Gately. The token needs the Cloudflare Tunnel: Edit permission, plus DNS: Edit on the zones to create DNS records automatically. Create a token at
ingressNeedsApi: Fill in an API token in the tunnel settings first

ingress.title: Routes · {name}
ingress.help: Rules are matched in order by hostname and path (regex); a request goes to the service of the first matching rule. Running tunnels apply changes automatically. Tunnel ID: {id}
ingress.localSource: This tunnel runs from a local config file, so remote routes on Cloudflare take no effect
ingress.catchAllHelp: Used when no rule matches; defaults to http_status:404
ingress.dnsHelp: Creates a proxied CNAME record pointing to {target} for each hostname; existing records are left as they are
ingress.dnsConflict: Existing record {existing} was left as is; check it in Cloudflare
ingress.savedDnsIssues: Routes saved; some DNS records need attention
ingress.confirmLocal: This tunnel is currently managed by a local config file. Saving writes the routes to the Cloudflare remote config and switches the tunnel to remote management; routes in the local config file will no longer apply. Save anyway?
